title: Weekly jobs sometimes skip a whole week
statement:
Our scheduler calls buildkit.cron.next_run() after each run and after restarts. A job set for Tuesdays at 09:00 was pushed a full week out when the scheduler restarted on a Monday afternoon:

    >>> from datetime import datetime
    >>> from buildkit.cron import next_run
    >>> next_run('0 9 * * 2', datetime(2026, 9, 14, 10, 30))    # Monday 10:30
    datetime.datetime(2026, 9, 22, 9, 0)    # expected datetime.datetime(2026, 9, 15, 9, 0)
    >>> next_run('0 9 * * 2', datetime(2026, 9, 14, 8, 30))     # Monday 08:30
    datetime.datetime(2026, 9, 15, 9, 0)    # correct

Monthly jobs have the same problem: next_run('0 3 1 * *', datetime(2026, 9, 30, 4, 0)) returns 2026-11-01 03:00 instead of 2026-10-01 03:00. Daily schedules look fine. The module docstring is the spec: the earliest matching minute strictly after now. Please fix next_run() for all expressions. It must keep taking now as an argument and must not read the clock.
targetSkill: calendar search logic (cron next-run across day boundaries)
